mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment directly boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth above 100k, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, the Federal Reserve signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation supply shock regimes (CPIAUCSL > 300 and INDPRO < 100), declining industrial production signals a contraction in supply capacity that increases input costs and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances meeting the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL > 300 and INDPRO < 100), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of months with UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and CPI inflation (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) indicates a monetary policy response to high inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by slowing GDP growth), a decline in quarterly real GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an impending economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansion with declining GDPC1, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts directly correlates with stronger consumer confidence and construction sector activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring additional regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of months with HOUST growth above 10%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.
